name: What is the difference between a reverse osmosis system and a standard water filter?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a reverse osmosis system and a standard water filter?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in their filtration capabilities. Standard water filters, like pitcher filters or faucet-mounted filters, typically use activated carbon to remove chlorine, sediment, and some organic compounds, improving taste and odor. A reverse osmosis system, however, utilizes a semi-permeable membrane in addition to carbon and sediment filters, allowing it to remove a much broader range of contaminants, including dissolved solids, heavy metals, fluoride, and even some bacteria and viruses. A practical tradeoff is that RO systems are more effective but also produce wastewater and require professional installation, unlike simpler filters. This makes RO a more comprehensive purification solution.
acceptedAnswer.description: RO systems use a membrane to remove a wider range of contaminants like dissolved solids and heavy metals, while standard filters mainly target chlorine and sediment.
